Subject: Edgeline.ai — free credits issuance flagged for cluster of similar devices

Hi Neha,

Quick heads up — our billing pipeline auto-issued free credits yesterday to a set of Edgeline.ai signups; I pulled a quick log and I'm seeing 14 accounts created across three days that share the same device fingerprint and a tight IP range. I attached the signup export (signup_logs_20270529.csv) and the device fingerprint JSON.

Given the patterns (rotating disposable email + identical device fingerprint), can Trust & Safety triage and advise whether we should rescind those grants? Sales is already talking to the Edgeline contact and I want to avoid giving credits that will be rapidly consumed by automation.

Related context: Edgeline asked for additional trial credits last week after some QA runs — their contact is Samuel Ortiz (samuel@edgeline.ai). I have not given any manual credits.

Ask: hold any additional automatic credit grants to edgeline.ai domains and let me know if we should mark the accounts for reversal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Edgeline.ai — free credits issuance flagged for cluster of similar devices

Kimberly / Neha,

Thanks for the ping — I pulled the records and started a quick triage. Findings so far (summary):
- 14 accounts created between 2027-05-27 and 2027-05-29.
- Shared device_fingerprint hash (attached) across 12 of the 14 accounts.
- Signups originated from 3 adjacent IPs in the same /24; reverse DNS inconsistent with the Edgeline public infra.
- Email addresses use rotating plus-addressing and several disposable domains (fastmail-proxy-type).
- Token consumption spike: average tokens used in first 24h is 9x our normal trial baseline for similar account cohorts.

Recommendation: place the 14 accounts into manual hold pending confirmation from the customer, revoke recently issued trial credits (or quarantine those tokens) and open a JIRA (TRUST-4821) for full evidence capture. We should also temporarily add an issuance rule to throttle auto-grants to edgeline.ai for 48 hours.

I attached the device_fingerprints_20270529.json and a short export. If Sales confirms these are legitimate internal QA signups, we can convert them into a single org account and reallocate credits.

Hi Samuel,

Hope you're doing well. I'm Kimberly on the Redwood team — we noticed some trial credits were auto-issued to multiple accounts that appear to be associated with Edgeline.ai activity. Our ops team flagged a cluster of 14 signups that share a device fingerprint and show unusually high token consumption in their first 24 hours. To avoid disruption we put the related credits on temporary hold.

Could you confirm whether those signups were internal QA/dev tests your team ran (e.g., ephemeral accounts for load testing) or legitimate separate end-users? If they're internal tests, happy to consolidate into a single org seat and extend a trial pool; if they're separate customers, we'll continue the investigation.

I've attached the list of account emails we flagged and the device fingerprint summary for reference. If you prefer, we can set a short call — Neha (our security lead) and Dev (Trust & Safety) are looped for triage.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can either release credits or proceed with remediation.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Quick clarification — Edgeline.ai trial signups and issued credits

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the noise.

Short answer: those were likely internal QA sessions. Our QA team spun up a batch of ephemeral test accounts last week while validating a new ingestion pipeline; they were using a small pool of cloud IPs and ephemeral emails from our test harness. We should have notified you — that's on us.

If you can provide the list of flagged account emails (you attached a CSV) we'll confirm which are ours and which are genuine external signups. We're open to consolidating into an org-level trial and taking a phone call with Sales to discuss enterprise options and committed usage.

Can you also confirm whether automatic refunds/revocations will impact analytics for any ongoing deals? We don't want a reversion to look like churn; if possible, place the reversal into a quarantined bucket that Sales can annotate.

Regards,
Samuel Ortiz
Head of Platform QA, Edgeline.ai
samuel@edgeline.ai
